Hands down one of the best habit trackers that I’ve found out there. The user interface is very intuitive and easy to use. It has absolutely everything I was looking for.
1. Ability to set daily, weekly or monthly goals.
2. Ability to create a goal that requires multiple completions to count toward a streak (i.e. taking meds—you can create two instances that go toward one goal).
3. Reminders that you can create to help you remember to complete your goal. Let’s face it some of us get busy and lose track of things we want to do during the day and this helps immensely.

These functions are in the pro version which is completely worth it, without a doubt.

I first downloaded HabitKit in the ending of March 2025. I bought the lifetime premium version. When I first downloaded the app, it didn't have an option for putting your own emojis for habits, which was really frustrating. I'm very happy that they finally put an emoji update. I was tired of using a dog bone for my seafood habit. My issue with the new update is that you can't change the skin color of the emojis. It's also disappointing that you can't choose a set of Crayola like colors for your habits including brown, instead of the preset pastel colors that is given. No true red or solid purples just a pastel palette for everything... I also think that the counter for 1, 5, 10 , 15 shouldn't be there. I think that instead the only option should be to set your own number of "Pages read" for each habit. It would look much better for the eyes that way. Or at least give the option to turn it off and only have your own preset number. I also think that the HabitKit wrapped should be worded better and upgraded. Besides those things, this is a decent app for habit tracking. I do also believe having a bad habit tracker section or page would be great, and helpful for separation of good and bad habits. Plus not being able to sync to iCloud is hella wack. I can only give 2 stars because I know it could be better.

title.label: The Perfect App For What I Needed

content.label:
This app on my phone has been insanely helpful and so easy to use. I can track anything going on in my life and then easily look back over the history of my habit. Things like how frequently I’m vacuuming or if I took my medication each day or week. Every time I login and track my habits it also reminds me of things I might not have done yet like…oh I haven’t done that thing yet today. So I often get up to start or finish something because I see that it isn’t checked off for the day. 

What makes this app better than others I was looking at is that I’m 100% choosing my own categories and specific tasks. So my weird and wonderful lists are tailored perfectly to me, and there isn’t anything extraneous. 

The only complaint I have is that the data is only on your device. So I can see and use it on my phone but I can’t pull it up on my tablet or computer. I reached out to the developers and they say they hope to change this in the future. So fingers crossed, this app could get even better.

Clean UI, no ads, and solid functionality that really motivates you to keep up on your goals! Best of all is a one-time payment alternative to the pro features instead of a forced subscription. Love it!

title.label: Best habit app you will find!

content.label:
I’ve genuinely tried all the habit apps- simple ones, complex ones, gamified ones, expensive ones — and HabitKit is easily the best of the bunch.

The grid based visual tracking is brilliant. It’s simple, motivating, and incredibly satisfying to look at. No unnecessary fluff, no overwhelming features- just a beautifully designed system that actually makes you want to stay consistent.

Customization is excellent, the UI is clean and intuitive, and it strikes the perfect balance between powerful and easy to use. This is the first habit app I’ve stuck with long term.

If you’re serious about building habits (or breaking bad ones), stop searching. HabitKit is it.
